company.name: Reelwick
company.tagline: Six people, one product, and one Companion Core in the comms room.
company.story: Reelwick writes schedule and rota software for independent cinemas. Six people share one brick bay. The code, the handbook, the contact list and the logins all sit on one Companion Core.

hookLine: Where does your customer list live?
arc: Six people, one list. The founder writes what the company rents on the whiteboard; the CTO, who is the one who installs the apps, moves the working memory of the company (code, contacts, handbook, logins) onto one shelf. Edge: the product itself runs where it runs; a security questionnaire from a first big customer is a different problem and is not touched.
honestEdge: The product runs in a cloud account that the Core does not replace. What moved is the company's own working memory.

building.concept: Converted brick warehouse bay: red brick, arched steel windows, parapet, closed neighbour bay (spike exists, 0 shot errors).

core.surface: wall shelf, chalk Core on a blue-grey wall, no books on the shelf
core.note: Make the Comms Room 3.6 x 3.6 m (the spike's 3 x 3 m gave foreground-occluder 31 percent and a 51.5 degree finale lens). No openings on its perimeter walls.

building.route: street door (double leaf with transom), Entry Lobby, along the bench of the Open Office, a glimpse of the glass Meeting Room, the Comms Room door, orbit.

rooms.name: Neighbour Workshop
rooms.note: closed bay, blinds, party wall door null

objectProps: whiteboard list of rented tools, brick bay with bike, device shelf in the comms room

lens.tone: Short dry bursts to peers, warm and exact with clients. Opens on a concrete noun.
lens.aiStance: Pragmatic. Wants drafts and answers from her own files. Proud of a chore done, not of having AI.
lens.honestLimit: No payroll, card processing or bank feeds; backup is the company's job; one Core is one owner's.

lens.tone: A bug report: short, exact, a little dry. Distrusts adjectives, respects a stated limit.
lens.aiStance: Heavy daily use, conditional trust. Wants checkable chores; fears the almost-right answer.
lens.honestLimit: He is the Core's admin on top of the job; never a CI run on screen; no parity or speed claims.

companion.name: Rivet
companion.job: Drafts pull request notes from commit messages Anselm pastes in.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Anselm reads every line before it is used.

lens.tone: Fragments, jargon, deadpan. "Repo is on the Core."
lens.aiStance: Uses it most days, does not brag, wants the diff.
lens.honestLimit: Whether work code moves is the company's decision; no CI run; no hosted-model parity.

lens.tone: Visual, opinionated, short. Reads terms updates like contracts.
lens.aiStance: The most guarded about generative AI. Practical about retouching, wary of generation. Do not push AI.
lens.honestLimit: Penpot is a tool, not a Figma migration; files an outside client must open stay on the office network.

lens.tone: Quick, numbers first, upbeat on the surface and dry underneath.
lens.aiStance: Heaviest adopter and proudest by reputation [?]; script slower than they talk.
lens.honestLimit: Reps away from the office are out of every scene; the CRM is the office's, not a per-rep platform account.

lens.tone: Brisk, list-making, kind. Triages out loud. Humour about the printer.
lens.aiStance: Quiet user for notices and summaries. Not proud, not hiding. [?] no role survey
lens.honestLimit: Accounts are made app by app by whoever looks after each app; the Core is not a managed service.

beats.title: A parcel at the brick door
beats.seed: A parcel waits by the bike rack outside the brick bay. Kofi carries it past the open office to the comms room, where Anselm clears a shelf.

beats.title: Unbox the Companion Core
beats.seed: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Femi lifts the Core out, and Anselm reads the guide.
beats.limit: Show exactly the box contents (claims core-in-box), nothing else.

beats.title: Plug it in
beats.seed: Anselm plugs in the cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.
beats.limit: note: Companion OS is in beta.

beats.title: Join it from a phone
beats.seed: Anselm opens the Wi-Fi settings on his phone and joins the Core's own network. Then he chooses the office network.
beats.limit: phone rows: Join the Core's own network; Choose the office network; Enter its password

beats.title: Pick the first agent and apps
beats.seed: In the Companion Hub store, Anselm picks Hermes, and the team adds Forgejo and Docmost. Then they get back to work.
beats.limit: note: Installing apps uses the internet.

beats.title: Rivet says hello
beats.seed: Anselm messages the agent he named Rivet from his desk. Rivet answers from the Core in the comms room.
beats.limit: note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: anselm
say.text: Hello, Anselm. I draft, and you decide.

beats.capabilityHint: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.title: A status page by the router
beats.seed: Uptime Kuma checks the office printer and the staging site. Anselm reads its page each morning before the others arrive.
beats.limit: Monitors, does not prevent. No uptime claim. Notifications leave through an outside channel only if set. Do not describe the screen. No replaces chip: the market review marks Datadog and New Relic a stretch (full observability suites), and a sceptic would not say it.
beats.capabilityHint: Watch your sites and services and get an alert when one goes down.

beats.title: One vault for shared logins
beats.seed: The shared logins leave a sticky note under a keyboard and move into VaultWarden. Anselm deletes the export file afterwards.
beats.limit: Say "the Bitwarden apps". Attachments and one-time-code seeds do not move; importing twice duplicates; delete the export file.

bringHome.carries: logins, notes and cards the import maps
bringHome.doesNot: file attachments; item history; shared-vault structure

beats.capabilityHint: Store every password in a vault you host. Works with the Bitwarden apps.

beats.title: The code moves in
beats.seed: Anselm moves the company's repositories into Forgejo on the Core. The product still runs where it runs; the code now sits in the comms room.
beats.limit: Say where the repositories are. Never "syncs with" or "compatible with" GitHub. No CI runner ships: never show a CI run. Actions workflows do not carry over. One Git host per office.

bringHome.carries: repository code and history; issues and pull requests when a token allows
bringHome.doesNot: Actions workflows; stars and followers; Discussions, Projects, Pages

beats.capabilityHint: Host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core.

beats.title: The note and the diff
beats.seed: Rivet drafts the pull request note from the commit messages Femi pastes to it. Anselm reads the diff, edits the note and posts it himself.
beats.limit: Agent prepares, person approves (beat needs agent + approval). Hermes is beta; the chat channel is not local. No parity or speed claim. Hermes is isolated from Forgejo: it works from pasted text only.
beats.capabilityHint: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.title: The screens sit on the Core
beats.seed: Anika draws the schedule screens in Penpot on the Core. The design files sit in the same room as the code.
beats.limit: No verified Figma importer: components were rebuilt by hand. Five containers. Do not describe the screen.

bringHome.carries: nothing automatic; Anika rebuilt the components by hand

beats.capabilityHint: Design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host.

beats.title: Every lead in one list
beats.seed: Kofi loads last quarter's cinema contacts into Twenty from a spreadsheet. The pipeline now sits on the Core, not in a rented CRM.
beats.limit: Never show Twenty's own QA capture (real company names). AGPL plus commercial files: never "open source". Automations, reports, sharing rules do not move. HubSpot users: no route, say nothing.

bringHome.carries: accounts, contacts and opportunities as CSV rows with relations mapped
bringHome.doesNot: flows and triggers; reports and dashboards; sharing rules; activity history

beats.capabilityHint: Keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself.

beats.title: The sprint board
beats.seed: The sprint board is a Planka board on the Core. Femi moves a card to done when the review closes.
beats.limit: Trello board JSON carries lists, cards, labels, checklists, comments; attachments and members unverified. Licence unasserted: do not call it open source.

bringHome.doesNot: Power-Ups and automations; attachments and members (check one board first)

beats.capabilityHint: A real-time Kanban board for a team or a family project.

beats.title: The office channel
beats.seed: The team talks in Campfire on the office network. Each person has an account inside Campfire, which is Campfire's own feature.
beats.limit: Write "integrations", never "bot API". First run creates an account in the app. The old channel history stays where it was (no verified importer): say what did not come along.

bringHome.carries: nothing: no verified importer for Campfire
bringHome.doesNot: channel history stays at the old service

beats.capabilityHint: Simple team chat with rooms, direct messages and a bot API.

beats.title: The shared drive moves in
beats.seed: Anika copies the shared drive into Nextcloud on the Core. Pitch decks and the logo folder come across; the share links do not.
beats.limit: No co-editing claim; sharing with outsiders not claimed; the importer talks to the old service while it runs. Share links and version history do not come across.

bringHome.carries: files and folders with names and structure
bringHome.doesNot: sharing settings; comments and suggestion history; version history

beats.capabilityHint: Your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices.

beats.title: A hand-off, built by hand
beats.seed: When Kofi marks a lead won in Twenty, n8n adds a card to the onboarding board. Femi rebuilt each step by hand.
beats.limit: Say "source-available", never "open source". Zaps are rebuilt by hand; connections are authorised again. Never "emails customers automatically".

bringHome.carries: the idea of each automation, rebuilt
bringHome.doesNot: Zap definitions, run history, connection tokens

beats.capabilityHint: Connect your apps with workflows. 400 plus integrations, with the data staying on your Core.

beats.title: Everything the company rents
beats.seed: Marit writes every rented tool on the whiteboard. Odile keeps the same list in Wallos on the Core, with the renewal dates.
beats.limit: No price, no saving, no total. Wallos fetches service logos from outside: do not show logos. No chip beyond the app name.
beats.capabilityHint: Track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews.

beats.title: Day one, one handbook
beats.seed: The handbook lives in Docmost. A new starter reads it on her first morning, at her own desk, with Odile beside her.
beats.limit: Overlaps BookStack (name one wiki per office). Notion export carries pages and structure; comments, history, sharing and databases do not.

bringHome.carries: page text and nested structure; images and files in the export
bringHome.doesNot: comments and page history; sharing; databases (arrive as CSV)

beats.capabilityHint: A collaborative wiki for notes and documentation.

beats.title: The flow, sketched
beats.seed: Anika and Femi sketch the schedule flow in Excalidraw on the wall screen. Anika exports a picture when they are done.
beats.limit: amd64 only.Miro boards are redrawn, not converted: a picture and the text of the sticky notes come across. Excalidraw here is the editor plus a collaboration relay with no storage volume: it keeps nothing on the Core. Never "saved", "kept" or "sits on the Core"; no bring-your-data-home beat for it.
beats.capabilityHint: A whiteboard with a hand-drawn look. Sketch ideas together.

beats.title: Signed at the table
beats.seed: Kofi and a cinema owner sign the pilot letter at the meeting table. DocuSeal keeps the signed copy on the Core.
beats.limit: Never "legally binding" or "valid". The signer is in the room: signers outside the office cannot reach the Core.
beats.capabilityHint: Fill and sign PDF forms on any device, from your own Core.

beats.title: A question for the files
beats.seed: Kofi asks a model on the Core what the pilot letter says about notice. AnythingLLM answers from the files, and he reads the clause himself.
beats.limit: Local model only; never mention a key. No accuracy, speed or parity claim. Avoid the listing's "multi-user" and "privacy-first" words.
beats.capabilityHint: Chat with your own documents and run agents with web browsing, with several users and permissions.

beats.title: Receipts, searchable
beats.seed: Odile feeds the month's receipts through the scanner into Paperless-ngx. Every page is read, and she finds a supplier's invoice by one word.
beats.limit: PDFs and scans only. AI features off by default. Never bare "Paperless". Email, the bank and the pay service stay with the services that run them.
beats.capabilityHint: Scan and file your paperwork. It reads every page, tags it and makes the lot searchable.

beats.title: The week by the kettle
beats.seed: Marit lays the week out in Companion Planning on the Core. Stand-up is at nine, and the printed week hangs by the kettle.
beats.limit: An owner's planner, not a team calendar (one owner account). Google sync is off by default; do not say it never touches Google. Crash-report disclosure applies.
beats.capabilityHint: Plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core. Briefings from a local model are optional.

beats.title: Her own notes, her own file
beats.seed: Marit keeps her own notes and calendar in Companion Memory (beta). It is one person's file, and she chooses what goes in.
beats.limit: Beta, first mention reads "(beta)". One person's context; imports opt-in; crash reports on by default; never "company brain".
beats.capabilityHint: Companion Memory keeps your digital life on your own disk, so your agents know your context and a cloud does not.

beats.title: Your turn next
beats.seed: The company's code, notes, contacts and logins now sit in one comms room. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.
beats.limit: closing body; the site and the film add the sign-off and the CTA.

disclosuresRequired: synthetic-voice (when the tour has a voice)
doNotSay: the product is hosted on the Core
writerRules: one person, one room, one app per beat; chip row is the app name then "replaces <service>" from the catalog entry
title at most six words, body at most thirty, sentence at most twenty, no digit, no dash, no exclamation mark, full stop
no UI mockup, no screen described, no customer, no price, no result, no time or capacity claim
the agent prepares and a person approves; one companion, on the Core's owner
every scene stays in the building on the office network; no remote, hybrid, mobile, public link or client portal
per-app accounts only, named as that app's own feature; never a Companion account per person
say what did not come along in every bring-your-data-home beat
sentence case; sign in, not log in; agent, not assistant; Companion Core, Companion Hub store

a file moves between apps by a person's hand (download, copy, file it), never by an integration: LibreOffice, Inkscape, Stirling-PDF, BentoPDF and draw.io keep nothing on the Core; never "goes straight into", "syncs to" or "lands in" another app (skeptic)
Hermes runs isolated from the other apps: it works from what a person types or pastes to it, never from a repository, a wiki or a drive it "reads" (skeptic)

capabilityHint strings are the catalog's own words and are never scanned by the validator: do not paste them into a title, body, caption or note; they hold words the canon bans (private, sandbox, QR code, bot API, nothing is uploaded, not sent to a third party, stays on your Core) (skeptic)
no sentence puts a head count and the Core together as "N people on one Core"; the Core belongs to one owner and the apps keep their own sign-ins (skeptic)
a replaces chip is the store's own pair; where a beat below carries no chip it is deliberate (skeptic: Uptime Kuma, Cryptgeon and LibreOffice pairs the briefs' own limits contradict)

changes: arc: "Seven people become six" read as a person replaced (biz-people-replaced by implication); now "Six people, one list."
comms-status: dropped "replaces Datadog" (market review: stretched; a CTO would not say it)
open-review and Rivet's job: Hermes "reads the commits" implied an integration the store says does not exist (Hermes runs isolated from other apps); now pasted text

meet-draw: "The sketch is saved on the Core" is false (compose has editor + collaboration relay, no storage volume); seed rewritten, bring-your-data-home flag removed (Miro to Excalidraw has no home on the Core)
planka licence note: upstream LICENSE.md is the PLANKA Community License (Fair Use License 1.1), not "unasserted"

hook line and titles: "stay in the office/studio/shop" is a place claim wider than the canon's "sits on the Core" (and a sent newsletter hands its addresses to the mail provider); now "sit on the Core"
